title: Control plane on-prem deploy lifecycle notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, incremental journal/runbook for on-prem (VPC & air-gapped) control-plane provisioning, horizontal scaling, and rolling upgrades. It compiles the field-tested sequences we used during the last three customer pilots, along with terraform module notes and quick rollback heuristics.

Audience:
- SREs and platform engineers executing day-zero provisioning or version upgrades
- Solutions engineers prepping customer cutovers
- Devs who will run canaries or validate network connectivity

Scope / Assumptions:
- Target cluster runs k8s 1.25+; control-plane components are containerized (operator + API + ingress).
- Terraform modules referenced are in private-cp-modules repo (see linked PR).
- Customer provides: VPC subnets, on-prem firewall rules, DNS zone, KMS/HSM creds, and a bastion host.
- This doc focuses on sequence and operational heuristics, not exhaustive terraform reference docs.

Preflight checklist (run before any infra change):
- Network: verify CIDR plan, confirm no overlapping VPCs, confirm required ports open (TCP 443, 10250, ephemeral for node healthchecks).
- DNS: customer zone delegated or Customer DNS admin provided credentials for A/ALIAS records.
- Time: ensure NTP is reachable; control-plane certs are time-sensitive.
- KMS/HSM: validate key ARN + policy, test an encrypt/decrypt using sample CLI call.
- Artifact access: ensure devices/mirrors have access to container registry (or provide airgapped bundle).
- Terraform: install TF v1.6.x (we pin to 1.6 in modules), provider plugins verified in .terraform.lock.hcl.
- Backups: snapshot DB or stateful stores; export current kube manifests if migrating.

Terraform module notes (pragmatic tips):
- Module: network.vpc (version 0.9.1+) expects "private_subnets" as list(string). Passing a map breaks az affinity; use simple list.
- Module: kms.key (0.4.0) will create a symmetric key by default. For HSM-backed keys, set create=false and pass key_arn.
- Module: controlplane.cluster (v1.3.2) has a boolean var "airgapped". If true, module will skip registry egress checks and provision an internal image mirror config.
- State: use remote backend (s3-compatible) with server-side encryption; for fully airgapped installs we still recommend an object-store reachable from the bastion for state sync.
- tfvars snippet we used in pilot: 
  region = "us-west-2"
  azs = ["us-west-2a","us-west-2b"]
  controlplane_count = 3
  node_pool_size = 6
  airgapped = false

Provisioning sequence (safe ordering):
1) Infra layer (terraform): network.vpc -> s3/bucket -> kms (create or attach) -> loadbalancer (internal)
2) Bootstrap infra: object-store + secrets-store (S3/minio + vault-lite)
3) DB & stateful stores: create postgres, redis clusters (provision with retention snapshot policy)
4) Control plane install: apply controlplane.cluster module with replicas=1 first (bootstrap), let leader initialize DB schema
5) Wait for leader readiness: check /healthz, DB migrations applied logs, cluster operator CRDs present
6) Scale control plane to desired replicas (usually 3) once leader is healthy
7) Install ingress/edge load balancing and external DNS entries
8) Install monitoring stack (prometheus scrape configs, alertmanager)
9) Run smoke tests and synthetic traffic generator for baseline latency/cost

Notes on step 4: start with replicas=1 on a non-prod tag to reduce blast radius. This lets DB migrations run under close observation. If migrations are idempotent, proceed to replicas=3. If not, follow migration window instructions in the related migration doc.

Scaling heuristics (horizontal & vertical):
- Horizontal scaling of control-plane components (API server replicas) should be driven by 95th percentile CPU and average request queue length. We used the following heuristics in pilot:
  - add replica when average queue length > 40ms and 95th CPU > 65% for 5m window
  - remove replica when queue length < 10ms and 95th CPU < 30% for 10m window
- Node pool scaling: prefer adding GPU nodes for throughput-bound workloads; use taints/tolerations to schedule only inference workloads there.
- Autoscaler: we recommend Cluster-Autoscaler with a conservative scale-down delay (10m) for stability.

Rolling upgrades and version compatibility:
- Compatibility matrix is in CONFLUENCE:CP-operator-design-2025 but the practical rule: don't jump more than 2 minor k8s/operator versions in a single upgrade wave.
- Canary upgrade process:
  1. Create a canary control-plane replica pool (label: upgrade=canary) with new image tag
  2. Route 3–5% of traffic to canary via edge LB rules or weight on ingress
  3. Monitor error rates, p99 latency, and auth failures for 30–60 minutes
  4. Promote to full rollout if stable, otherwise rollback canary and capture logs
- Upgrade order recommended: operator -> api -> ingress -> agents. Reason: operator applies DB migrations and reconciliation logic that must be present before newer API versions send traffic.

TLS / Cert rotations and KMS key rotations:
- TLS cert rotation sequence: generate cert -> stage on 1 replica -> verify mutual TLS / client cert acceptance -> roll other replicas. Always keep previous cert overlap period of 24h where both certs are valid to avoid connection resets.
- KMS rotation: rotate by creating a new key, re-encrypt secrets, and update secret-store references. Test decrypt with the new key on a non-prod pod before switching.

Example commands (operational):
- Terraform plan/apply: 
  cd infra/modules/controlplane && terraform init -backend-config=... && terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars && terraform apply -var-file=prod.tfvars
- Draining a node prior to replacement: kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=30m
- Rolling restart of control-plane deployment: kubectl rollout restart deploy/controlplane-api -n redwood-controlplane

Smoke tests (post-provision / post-upgrade):
- API health: curl -sS https://api.<customer-zone>/healthz -> expect 200 and JSON {"ready":true}
- Auth check: token mint + one signed call to user-info endpoint
- KV integrity test: write/read/delete 50 keys to secrets-store using KMS-wrapped secrets
- Latency regression: run load test with 100 req/s for 2m and assert p95 < baseline + 30%
- End-to-end inference smoke: send small prompt payload, assert complete response within SLO

Rollback heuristics (fast options):
- If new controlplane image causes error spikes and canary was not used: scale down new replicas and scale up previous image using kubectl set image or revert terraform module image tag.
- If DB migration fails mid-upgrade: restore DB from the pre-upgrade snapshot, mark upgrade failed in ticket, and escalate to oncall DB lead.
- Always collect full operator logs and a dump of CRDs before attempting rollback.

Failure modes and mitigation notes observed in pilots:
- KMS permissions error on bootstrap: root cause usually overly strict key policy. Mitigation: attach temporary admin key policy, complete bootstrap, then lockdown and create least-privilege policy post-provision.
- Image pull failure in airgapped installs: confirm mirror manifest and image digest match; fallback to local tarball import on bastion.
- Sudden token auth failures after upgrade: usually caused by clock skew between control-plane nodes and KMS; re-sync NTP and restart auth service pods.

Observability / validation dashboards to review immediately after change:
- Control-plane per-node CPU/RPS and API request latency (p99, p95)
- Auth errors (5xx vs 4xx split)
- DB migration lag and replication lag (seconds)
- TLS handshake failures per-minute

Security notes:
- Minimize broad IAM policies; prefer service role per control-plane component with least privilege.
- For airgapped installs, use signed container images and digest locking in terraform module (image_digest var).
- Ensure bastion logs are shipped to customer SIEM and redwood support has temporary, limited RBAC support tickets for escalation.

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- [ ] Add sample tfvars for HSM-backed KMS (blocked by customer HSM info).
- [ ] Standardize canary traffic steering using route weights in the ingress vs edge LB (follow up with networking team).
- [ ] Document a streamlined emergency rollback plan that does not require DB restore for non-migrative releases.

Notes to self / field tips:
- When in doubt, bring up a single replica with verbose logs (LOG_LEVEL=debug) and run the smoke test loop locally from bastion; quicker than chasing ephemeral logs.
- Keep a small test harness (k6 script + token mint) in the repo for consistent post-change validations.

History / provenance:
- Composed from notes across three pilot installs (Q2–Q3 2025) and the GH PR referenced above. This remains intentionally terse; expand into a full-runbook if this lifecycle proves repeatable across multiple customers.

If you run this: please tag slack #private-deploys with timestamps and a link to applied terraform plan output. That log has saved us twice when needing to reconstruct drift sequences.

-- Asha
